notes: One record per card, keyed by Scryfall `oracle_id`: a front-face name is not an identifier, so a name key moves every card that answers to it (review finding D1). `name` is an assertion, not data — the run fails when an `oracleId` no longer names the card written beside it. `why` is the curation rationale. `plane` is an Appendix A slug. PRD 11.9 orders the curation work; a record that matches no first printing is listed in the run report rather than applied.

rule: A record is written only when the card's own printed front face identifies exactly one plane: a plane named in flavour text or in the card name, a location or faction exclusive to one plane, a creature type exclusive to one plane, or a named character with one plane of origin. The evidence is read off the front face only — the committed records were curated that way, so a back face's flavour text, type line or character is not grounds for a record and a transforming card is judged on its front alone (review note N3). Cards naming two planes (a cross-plane team-up, or an event that travels between worlds) and cards whose text says 'the Multiverse' are left in the Blind Eternities on purpose — the dust is the correct answer for a card with no single setting (PRD 4.7.3), not a bucket to be emptied. `why` carries the evidence so a reviewer can audit a line without opening Scryfall.
